evidence_scope_law: The deterministic assemble-shard step canonicalizes shard evidence_span_ids as at least the complete union of every node and claim citation before validation; model-proposed root scope is not authoritative.
semantic_id_law: Every model-authored identifier is lowercase ASCII kebab-case matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$; human-language labels belong in name, aliases, summary, reason, or properties rather than IDs.
node_id_law: Every node_id begins with its exact node_kind plus a hyphen, for example npc-kloppe.
source_language_law: source_language identifies the language of the parsed source artifact. All model-authored semantic prose, including name, aliases, summary, reason, and prose-valued semantic properties, remains in that source language. The graph compiler never translates it. A later Keeper presentation layer may localize output to play_language without mutating this graph.
coverage_law: Only declared aspects may be accepted, partial, or absent. Every undeclared aspect is exactly unresolved because that extraction did not review the domain.

ordering_law.print-precedes: Only the publication order. When the source explicitly presents an ordered list of playable units, preserve adjacent order as traversable print-precedes claims and relations rather than relying on JSON array order.
ordering_law.play-precedes: Only a source-supported recommended or required play order.
ordering_law.triggers: A causal dependency, never inferred from array or chapter order.
ordering_law.independent-from: Anthology or sidetrack members that do not form one task chain.

classification_fields.law: A classification field holds the product's own category for a fact the book states, which the book does not itself name in these terms. An independent review may contest it: the reader's value is published with a contested mark carrying the reviewer's reason, and the Keeper sees the mark. A classification field never refuses a record; only a fact the page does not state does (contract 22.3.2). Patterns are JSON pointers relative to a node (/nodes/<i>); * stands for any one token.

actor_dossier.why: An npc is a being the Keeper plays as a person: the book gives the investigators a way to deal with it as someone (talk, bargain, persuade, argue it down, call its name), and it has a name to learn and motives of its own. It stays an npc when it is a monster, a ghost or a captive alien that answers questions, and when it does not speak. A being the book presents only as a body is a creature (creature_dossier). The kind is decided per node and per encounter from how the book treats the being, never per species (contract §180.2). A stat block is not a person (contract §17.2). These are the words the extraction vocabulary uses for what a book says about someone as a person, so the reader prompt, the starter projector, the playability brief and the table all read one list instead of each keeping their own.
actor_dossier.profile_labels_why: The Keeper-facing name each profile key arrives under in the turn capsule's `present` dossier, and the order it arrives in. It lives beside the keys so the table reads the same spine the reader prompt, the starter projector and the brief read, instead of keeping its own copy; a key with no label here arrives under its own name.
actor_dossier.prose_keys_why: Prose an actor speaks or the keeper reads stays in `properties`: a claim's object is a node, never a sentence.
actor_dossier.law: Every name here already exists in `relation_kinds`; this block groups them by what they are for and adds no vocabulary. A key a book does not give is absent, never invented -- an actor with none is reported by the measure `npcs_without_material` and fails nothing.

creature_dossier.why: A creature is a being the book presents only as a body: an animal, a swarm, a mindless monster, or a mind that never deals with anyone. A being the book lets the investigators deal with as someone is an npc (actor_dossier), even when it is a monster. The kind is decided per node and per encounter from how the book treats the being, never per species: one species can be an npc in one encounter and a creature in another; a life stage the book gives its own numbers is its own node; a parasite with its own body and numbers is a creature beside its host; a being with a human and a monstrous form is one npc (contract §180.2). These are the words for what a book says about a creature, the counterpart of actor_dossier. It has no core keys; a package adds its words here (contract §180.8).
creature_dossier.law: A key a book does not give is absent, never invented. The person words of actor_dossier are not asked of a creature (contract §180.4). One being is one node: an npc and a creature never share a normalized name or handle (contract §180.7).

actor_weaknesses.why: Contract §180.9: what the book says harms, repels, binds, banishes or ends an npc or creature, the means it names, and the conclusion through which the investigators can learn it. A build binds it only when an enabled package requires `actor.weaknesses.v1`; the reader's task then carries this block, and the draft check holds every entry to it.
actor_weaknesses.law: `book` (required) is one English line in the book's terms saying what harms, repels, binds, banishes or ends the being, with its conditions and degree; a stat-line resistance belongs here too, never in keeper_note. `needs` lists the node ids of the means the book names; a controller whose end ends the being is an npc here, and one means may appear on many beings. `learned_by` is the id of the conclusion the investigators can reach that states the weakness, supported by the clues that teach it; it is absent when the book gives no route, and such a weakness is the Keeper's alone, found in play. What the book does not give is absent, never invented.

relation_endpoints.why: Contract §180.9: a relation kind whose meaning holds only between certain node kinds. A claim of a kind listed here connects only the kinds listed for it.
relation_endpoints.law: `misleads` marks a clue whose belief about an npc or creature is false. A false lead against a weakness the book also states truly is the existing clue --contradicts--> that weakness's conclusion.
